stem: After administering an injection with a safety-engineered needle device, what should the nurse do next?

options.A: Engage the safety feature and immediately place the device in an appropriate sharps container
options.B: Recap the used needle with both hands before disposal
options.C: Leave the safety feature unused if no blood is visible on the device
options.D: Keep the used device at the bedside until the end of the shift

rationale: CDC sharps-safety guidance states that immediately after a sharp is used, any safety feature should be engaged and the device placed in an appropriate sharps disposal container. OSHA defines safety-engineered sharps as engineering controls intended to reduce exposure incidents. Therefore A is the best action. Two-handed recapping increases needlestick risk, safety-feature activation is not conditional on visible blood, and delaying disposal leaves a contaminated sharp accessible.
educational_objective: Use safety-engineered sharps correctly by engaging the safety mechanism after use and disposing of the device immediately in an appropriate sharps container.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) / National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH)
source_document_title: Sharps Disposal During a Mass Vaccination Campaign — Healthcare Workers
source_locator: Sharps disposal recommendations: immediately after use, engage any safety feature and place the sharp in a closable, puncture-resistant, leakproof, labeled/color-coded sharps disposal container; do not recap, break, bend, or separate contaminated needles before disposal
source_claim_supported: After use of a sharp, engage its safety feature and dispose of it immediately in an appropriate sharps container; avoid recapping or other manipulation that increases needlestick risk.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: use safety devices and infection-prevention practices to reduce client and healthcare-worker exposure to injury and infectious material
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — sharps safety / safety-engineered device use
correction_summary: Removed the vague statement that activation must occur 'before disposal' without a direct procedural locator and anchored the item to current CDC/NIOSH guidance: engage the safety feature immediately after use and immediately dispose in a sharps container. Distractors were rewritten around realistic unsafe sharps practices.
audit_findings: A directly matches current CDC/NIOSH sharps disposal guidance and is consistent with OSHA's engineering-control framework. B is unsafe two-handed recapping; C wrongly makes activation depend on visible blood; D delays disposal and leaves a contaminated sharp exposed. One best answer remains with no unsupported mechanism, cueing, or second-answer ambiguity.
